title: A Record Number of Black Candidates Are Running for Governor This Year
summary: Imagine if only three kids in your whole school had ever been class president—and they were all boys. That's kind of what it's been like for Black governors in America. In 250 years, only three Black people have been elected governor. But this year, that could change in a big way. Eight Black candidates are running for governor in different states. That's more than ever before! They are men and women, Democrats and Republicans. Some of them are Wes Moore in Maryland, Byron Donalds in Florida, and Lisa Demuth in Minnesota. Wes Moore is already the governor of Maryland. He says being the first Black governor is not just about applause. It's about fixing big problems. Many of the candidates don't talk much about race. They talk about their plans for jobs and schools. Byron Donalds said Florida is a great place where anyone can succeed. He didn't even mention his race in his victory speech. But other people say having Black governors matters a lot. Aaron Ford is running in Nevada. He says some issues in Black communities get ignored. He wants to focus on voting rights and the economy. Lisa Demuth says she never leads with identity politics. But she knows this is a historic moment. Former New York Governor David Paterson says this is a day when both parties can feel proud. He said we're finally getting it right. Some people think Black governors will be extra important now. The Supreme Court made a decision about voting districts. And President Trump has attacked diversity programs. Wes Moore says governors are becoming the last line of defense. Karen Finney helped Joe Biden pick a Black woman for vice president. She says Black politicians often speak up first about health problems like sickle cell disease. She says governors have power to shape our lives. So this November, history could be made. Will your state elect a Black governor? Keep an eye on the news!
why_it_matters: When you see leaders from different backgrounds running for governor, it shows that a kid from your community might grow up to make big decisions too.

keywords.explanation: A governor is like a president, but just for one state.
Candidates are people trying to be chosen for a job or office.
Identity politics means focusing on a person's race, gender, or background in politics.
Diversity programs are efforts to include people from many different races and backgrounds.
Voting rights are rules that protect people's ability to vote.
Sickle cell disease is an illness that changes red blood cells and can cause serious pain.

background_read: Only a few Black Americans have ever been governor, so many people call this year historic.
President Donald Trump (the U.S. president since 2025) has criticized some diversity programs, making them part of a big national argument.
The Supreme Court (the highest court in the U.S.) has also ruled on voting districts, which can affect whose vote counts.
Article_Structure: WHO: Eight Black candidates, including Wes Moore in Maryland, Byron Donalds in Florida, and Lisa Demuth in Minnesota.
WHAT: They are running for governor in different states, a record number that could change history this November.
WHERE: The races are taking place in several U.S. states, including Maryland, Florida, Minnesota, and Nevada.
WHY: Some candidates focus on jobs and schools, while others say Black governors matter for voting rights, the economy, and health issues.
